long_biography.plain_text:
Rhonda Wyllie helped finance a new investment venture when she and her daughter, Melissa Karlson, backed Marshall Allen and Craig Coleman in establishing Viburnum Funds in 2007. The partnership gave the family's capital a dedicated investment team. Wyllie's controlled group subsequently held a majority interest in Viburnum's Strategic Equities Fund.

Her charitable work has also focused on practical equipment. In 2021, she and her family funded a stem-cell robot for the Lions Eye Institute through a gift announced with Telethon. The machine was designed to automate cell cultures, allowing researchers to produce retinal tissue more efficiently for studies of inherited eye diseases.
